newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backeds tighten as Treasuries falter.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backeds tighten as Treasuries falter.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities prices were lower this session, but spreads to Treasuries tightened, said market participants.
Prices on discount mortgage coupons saw the most notable declines today -- some were off as much as 11/32 -- and premium coupon prices were down by 4/32 to 8/32.
"It was a quiet day," said a New York balloon trader. "We are seeing some interest in up-in-coupon activity.
If Treasury rates stay at current levels, the trader said, mortgage security spreads to Treasuries likely will continue to tighten.

Among active 30-year 7 1/2-percent issues, GNMA bonds were down 8/32 at 101-1/32 bid, FNMA 7.5 percent coupons were off 12/32 at 100 31/32 and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp.7.5 percent coupons were down 11/32 at 101-5/32.
Ten-year Treasury notes were 9/32 lower on the day at 102-29/32 to yield 6.22 percent.

Market players said premium coupons were not enduring as much selling pressure now that Treasury prices have fallen and prepayment fears have subsided. Prior to the large Treasury sell-off Friday, investors were selling off premium mortgage coupons, fearing prepayment risk.
Market players said there were not many trades Monday indicative of a long-term commitment to MBS. Investors, said one market observer, likely would be focused on this week's Treasury refunding.
The Treasury will sell $16 billion in three-year notes, $12 billion in 10-year notes and $10 billion in 30-year bonds on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

Thursday's July chain store sales data, said one market player, may be closely watched because it may offer clues about consumer demand. "If you were to see strength in consumer demand, the I would think that people who converted to the growth-without-inflation scenario may think twice," she said, adding that if fears of inflation are sparked, Treasuries may weaken.

Looking ahead, participants were also awaiting Federal National Mortgage Association and Government National Mortgage Association prepayment data due Thursday. This upcoming data, participants say, should show heightened prepayment activity in 8.0 percent and 8.5 percent coupons in the month of July. (( --Aleksandrs Rozens, N.A. Mortgage Unit, 212-859-1668 ))
